subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@finlytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-25T15:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - follow-up

Hi Alex - thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap and agreed next steps from our call so we have a single thread:

Summary of Finlytics requirements (as discussed)
- End-to-end latency targets: p95 and p99 for API responses (including any network hop between your app and inference). You mentioned these targets are critical for UX on your live agent.
- Streaming: client expects partial tokens via SSE/HTTP2 for progressive answers.
- Concurrency/QPS: steady-state ~150 QPS with expected concurrency of ~50 concurrent sessions; bursts up to 500 QPS around market open.
- Workload mix: 60% short prompts (~50 tokens), 40% long context (~1k tokens) with KV cache reuse.
- Current provider baseline: you said you have some numbers to share - please paste the CSV you exported (attachment).

Our immediate next steps
1) Please send the performance CSV and any request traces (you mentioned a perf-run export) - that will let us map your profile to Redwood's execution paths.
2) We'll propose a hosted POC profile (p95/p99 targets + test harness) and a Dedicated/Reserved config if you need guaranteed throughput.
3) If you're comfortable, share an allowlist of IPs and a short sample request set (anonymized) so we can reproduce end-to-end.

I'll put Aditya (perf lead) and Laura (AE) on this thread to help scope the POC.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

From: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-26T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - follow-up

Hi Marissa - thanks for the recap and for putting folks on the thread. Attached is the CSV export from our monitoring during yesterday's load window (perf-run-20261025.csv). Key numbers from our current provider (end-to-end as measured from our app servers to inference and back):
- Baseline p95: 420 ms
- Baseline p99: 980 ms
- Typical concurrency: 45-60 active sessions (peaks ~120 concurrent for short spikes)
- Average QPS: 140; peak burst saw ~520 QPS for ~4 minutes
- Streaming: currently using HTTP chunked responses; we need SSE support or chunked transfer to show partial answers in the UI.
- Payload sizes: short requests ~30-80 tokens, long ones up to ~1,200 tokens with 1K context overlap in many cases.

Constraints: we are regulated - logs/PII redaction is required for any test data. Please confirm what you need from our side and whether Redwood hosted will be able to match/beat the above p95/p99 numbers.

Also looping procurement (procurement@finlytics.com) - they may want to coordinate on a temporary MSA/PO for the POC.

Thanks,
Alex Thompson
Head of Platform Engineering | Finlytics
alex.thompson@finlytics.com

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Thompson <alex.thompson@finlytics.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-27T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Performance SLO (p95/p99) - hosted vs current provider - follow-up

Alex - appreciate the export and the clear numbers. Quick read on what we can commit for a hosted POC and options if you ultimately need Dedicated capacity.

Redwood hosted POC proposal (summary)
- Target SLOs (end-to-end, measured from your app): p95 <= 300 ms, p99 <= 650 ms for the short/median workload profile (50-80 token prompts). For the long-context profile (~1k tokens) we expect p95 <= 750 ms, p99 <= 1.4 s - those numbers assume typical network latency between your app and our hosted region.
- Streaming: full SSE and HTTP chunked streaming supported - we'll deliver partial tokens as they generate. We also offer TCP/HTTP2 streaming for lower overhead if you prefer.
- Concurrency & throughput: Hosted autoscaling can handle steady-state 150 QPS and transient bursts to 600 QPS for short windows. For consistent high concurrency with strict SLOs we recommend Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool) - we can size the pool after the POC.
- Measurement and instrumentation: We will run an end-to-end test harness using your anonymized sample traffic. We'll provide per-request timing (client-side, gateway, model inference, kernel exec) so you can see exactly where any tail latency originates.

Proposed POC plan (timeline)
1) Share anonymized request set + allowlist (you) - 48 hrs
2) Redwood runs a 24-72 hour POC with identical request mix - we run both hosted and (optional) dedicated equivalent and produce a comparison report - 5 business days
3) Joint review call to walk results, tuning, and sizing recommendations - 1 business day after POC

Deliverables
- POC perf report (CSV + PDF summary)
- p95/p99 breakdown by request bucket
- streaming latency measurements (time to first token and time to final token)
- recommendations for Dedicated sizing/quantization if needed

Next bits from you
- Confirm you can provide an anonymized sample set (or let us generate a synthetic load if redaction is a blocker).
- Confirm allowlist IPs we should use (we can also provide a short-lived API key and allowlist).

I've attached a short proposal PDF that outlines the hosted POC and a Dedicated sizing worksheet. If this looks good I'll put a formal POC scope in HubSpot and propose dates the week of Nov 9 for the run.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

--
Attachment: redwood-hosted-slo-proposal-20261030.pdf (proposal, 58KB)

Subject: Internal: Finlytics POC ask - perf baseline & next steps

Aditya/Laura - quick internal note summarizing Finlytics ask from thread (Finlytics / RDW-DEAL-8931):
- They reported p95 420 ms / p99 980 ms (end-to-end) for mixed workload. Steady-state ~140 QPS; bursts to ~520 QPS. Streaming required (SSE/HTTP chunked).
- I proposed Redwood hosted targets: p95 <= 300 ms, p99 <= 650 ms (short prompts); larger context will have higher tails. Hosted autoscale can hit their steady/peak, but Dedicated recommended for strict SLOs under sustained load.

Action items
- Aditya: please review the attached perf CSV and let me know what test harness config we should run to reproduce their numbers (model, batch size, quantization profile, kernel selection, region). Estimate: 24-72 hr POC with both hosted autoscale and a dedicated config.
- Laura: please prep a short POC SOW and pricing note we can send after we confirm test window. I'll draft the HubSpot POC and propose week of Nov 9.

HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/8931

Thanks - Marissa
